hills.description: The new program uses a multi-resolution approach: it starts from a resampled grid and applies block-multiplicative perturbations, edge-preserving smoothing, and global noise, rather than the record's single-resolution coordinate hill climb with a final line search. It also uses a fixed random seed and a 90% CPU deadline with a different perturbation mix (blocks, smoothing, noise) instead of the r…

This program optimises a smooth soft-max surrogate of the sup-norm (log-sum-exp with increasing sharpness β) via L-BFGS on a squared-parameterisation w↦w², rather than hill-climbing heights directly. It adds Anderson extrapolation on the fixed-point iteration to accelerate convergence, and it anneals β across three stages with repeated rounds per stage. It also seeds from several sine-power bumps…

This program optimises the full autocorrelation ratio directly via Dinkelbach iterations on a square-root variable with a soft-max surrogate for the infinity norm, rather than isolating the level-transition loss and perturbing along its gradient. Instead of gradient-guided perturbations, it explores by rank-ordering cells, zeroing or rescaling contiguous runs of the lowest 15% of heights, and zer…

This program seeds a hand-built spike-plus-decaying-comb shape and refines it with a Dinkelbach-style ascent that maximizes num − λ·l1·linf via random contiguous-block scaling, rather than starting from the record's symmetric construction and moving f along the transition-loss gradient. This program optimises a smooth soft-max surrogate of the sup-norm (exponential penalty with β annealed 500→2000→8000) via Dinkelbach iterations on a squared-weight parametrisation, rather than perturbing along a transition-loss gradient with shallow re-polishing.
